body:
For this task, we will be doing part A of the work described below:

The previous task (undo atomicity, WAL, crash hook) is finished and reviewed as "Looks good". Two pieces of work are left: A, the reader-side switch to computed changes, and B, subtask 4 (locks and agent_guard). After that, a few done-when tests and risks still need owners. Each task should start by reading D-77 and Spec 15, and cite D-17, D-18 and D-61 point 4 as amended.

A. Compute changes from the stores (follow-up to subtask 1)
Goal: the task JSON no longer stores changes (D-77 point 4). changes is computed from each scope project's store.db board_touches, by task id.

Where things stand:

board_touches now has run and name columns.
board::record only writes rows.
board::list_changes sends a changes message to the task server after COMMIT. This is a stopgap and should be removed.
Steps:

Add a changes_of(task) helper in board.rs. It reads board_touches from every project in the task's scope through a WAL read, with no lock, and returns {entity, run, name, project} in insertion order.
Use it in read_task_api (about board.rs:1290) so the API still returns changes. Clients don't change.
Switch every reader of t["changes"] over to it:
review_state
task_diff
revert's named
set_scope (E7013)
outside::absorb (outside.rs, about lines 312 and 517–519)
view::task_here (view.rs, about lines 348, 369 and 715)
the brief's changes section (about board.rs:2096)
Drop changes from new_task. Delete list_changes and the changes message type in tasks.rs. A changes message still in an old inbox should be ignored, not fail.
Make the one-time move (adopt_tasks) stop writing changes to the JSON. It already moves the entries into board_touches.
Tests:

New unit test: a revert while a changes message is still pending in inbox/. After the revert, applying the message adds nothing.
Acceptance: tasks from two projects keep their scopes, conversations and changes after the move, and undo works on them.
Both acceptance suites pass through rust-acceptance. Run rust-board-tests and rust-lockdown-tests as well.
B. Subtask 4: locks and agent_guard
Task-only actions take no project lock: create, edit, move (except into a final column), note, stop, cancel without undo, scope, and answers. They go only through the task server.

Code-changing actions keep the store lock of each project they touch:

undo
moving into a final column
approving settings
accepting outside changes
adding or removing a project
agent_guard: for task … commands it reads the run state from the task file with no lock. Update agent_guard_follows_the_run (about board.rs:3243).

Hazard from this subtask: once locks are relaxed, lockdown::recover must not adopt a live run's pending/run-<rid>.json or command-<rid>.json as a crashed one. Before adopting a record, check that its run is no longer running in the task file, or check who holds the lock.

Tests:

Create, note and stop each succeed in under about 1 s while a declared sleep 5 command runs.
A test for the recover/live-run hazard: start a declared run, then issue a second command on the same project, and check that the first run's rows are neither adopted nor duplicated.
C. Done-when tests and their owners
| Test | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A crash leaves neither the change nor its undo, or both | this subtask | done (4 crash tests) |
| A double create with one request id makes one task | subtask 2 | confirm it exists |
| An inbox message is applied after serve restarts | subtask 2 | confirm it exists |
| Two projects after the move, undo works | A | open |
| A revert with a pending changes message | A | open |
| agent_guard_follows_the_run updated | B | open |
| Create, note and stop under 1 s during sleep 5 | B | open |
| /events Last-Event-ID reconnect | subtask 2 | confirm it exists |

D. Risks to carry forward
A CLI run with no server leaves its notes in inbox/ until the next serve. Document this in the README.
Under WAL, every connection needs the 10 s busy timeout. A new Connection::open site that lacks it will fail with SQLITE_BUSY.
A long declared run doesn't hold the write lock, because the process runs outside the transaction. Long gleam check runs inside a command still do.
rust-lockdown-tests now exists. Run it alongside the other suites in A and B.
title: Task Store: Compute changes
